title: Fights, the Montutti nickname and the Odd Fellows funeral band
summary: Garland tells of breaking up a fight between cousins, nightly fights with Johnny Dodds, and fights over being called Montutti while playing bass drum in a lodge funeral band.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: That broke him off for a while, though. That boy hit him inside the nose. Did you slow him down a little bit?

He hit him, too. I don't blame him. He's a pretty old girl. I wasn't that bad. I got into Humberg and Rick Charles. Two cousins was fighting. I called myself trying to separate them and they thought I was interfering, gonna get in and help them and they hauled off and they beat me half to death, both of them. I also I said, man, what are you doing? I said, I'm trying to separate you boys. I don't care who it is. I don't want to see you boys fighting.
I don't want to see you boys fighting.
I said, I want to kill you. I said, I want to kill you.
I said, I want to do it out there.

Everybody on the best and I'm out there and I want to try to stop them boys from fighting. They black by. Me and Johnny Dodd took a fight every night. Really? Every night. We'd get the kid and get the best of them first thing in the fight. Right after the affair was over, we'd all go down there. Down probably we'd go down to the Pacawas or go somewhere to the Eagle Saloon drink and give us some oil saloon. Then we forgot all about the fight. Throw nobody in the fear though.

You and Johnny? Mm-hmm. What'd you fight about? You and Johnny say, start the kid and get the best of one another. They call me that Montutti, you know, and I didn't want them to call me that. I was playing in the Al Jays, a funeral for the odd fellas. There was twelve of us. And I'm back there, playing the bass drum. Come on, Montutti, what's the matter? I said, who you talking to? Come on, hit that drum, man. You're going to be tired. I'll be arguing over there, that guy.

Then it looked like it got way up there to some of the guys in the line in the back. Then they started to holler at Montutti. And there I was, joking so funny. Oh, come on there, Montutti. To-doot. And they had no bass drum at all to fight them all. Oh, man, I had a double of time carrying this name. And Lorenzo Stahls, I hauled off and hit him with my bass bow and broke it. You must have made a lot of fights. Oh, man, I had more fights than I got fingers and toes. Hmm. Ha, ha, ha, ha. First, then, all I had a good swallow with them all. But I'd all have money.
